newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Trade boost seen from Hong Kong/Philippines deal.
newsitem.headline: Trade boost seen from Hong Kong/Philippines deal.

text.p: More passengers and air cargo are expected to be flown between Hong Kong and the Philippines after negotiations on a new Air Services Agreement (ASA) finally reached a successful conclusion after six years, the Hong Kong government said.

However the number of new flights, and the planned increases in seat and cargo capacity included in the agreement is not being disclosed under the terms of the Confidential Memorandum of Understanding, industry sources said.
The breakthrough over what the Hong Kong government described as one of the busiest and fastest growing routes in Asia came during two days of talks in Hong Kong which ended on Wednesday.

Two previous rounds of talks earlier this year had ended in deadlock. The old ASA needed to be renegotiated before China takes over Hong Kong from British rule next July so flights were not threatened with being grounded, the observers added.

"This agreement provides a proper legal footing for the smooth continuation of air services between Hong Kong and the Philippines through and beyond 1997. It will assist both the development of our air services and further enhance the opportunities for trade and tourism between Hong Kong and the Philippines," Hong Kong's chief negotiator Michael Arnold said.
A spokesman for Hong Kong carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd welcomed the agreement.
"We are very pleased that the two sides have struck a deal. More seat capacity means more flights and more belly capacity for cargo. It is a very good foundation for the long term," he said.
Any new flights will have to wait until after the ASA is approved by the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG), set up to oversee Hong Kong's handover.
Cathay says it has no plans at the moment to increase its three times a day service to Manila and three times weekly flights to Cebu or to increase the number of destinations.
It also operates an overnight cargo service to Manila using empty Airbus A330 passenger aircraft full of belly cargo.

Sources close to the talks blamed the previous breakdown on flag carrier Philippine Airlines' insistence on being granted fifth freedom rights to pick up passengers in Hong Kong for their European bound flights.

Philippine Airlines has declined so far to comment on the new deal, while management at another airline represented at the talks, Manila-based all cargo carrier Pacific East Asia Cargo could not be contacted for imnmediate comment.

The Hong Kong government says it was the last ASA to be renegotiated before the handover and 13 ASA's have already been signed. The Joint Liaison Group has cleared four more for signature and a number of others are still awaiting approval including with key trade partners Japan and the U.S., a government statement said.
There has been concern that the ASA's may not be agreed in time for the handover, opening the potential flights being halted but the government says it is optimistic.

"We are confident that all the remaining agreements will be appproved by the JLG and signed well before the change of sovereignty in 1997,"Arnold said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
